ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the skier slides down to the right from point O at the upper left along a section of inclined plane, reaches the intersection point M of the inclined plane and the horizontal plane, then continues to slide along the horizontal plane to point N on the right and stops. In the figure, a vertical dashed line is drawn downward from point O, and there is also a vertical dashed line at point N; the horizontal arrow at the bottom marks the horizontal distance from the vertical projection of O to N as s. Then reason: Let the horizontal projection of the inclined-plane section be x, then the length of the horizontal section MN is s-x. On the inclined plane, the magnitude of the friction force is f1=μmg cosθ, and the length of the inclined plane is L, so the work done in overcoming friction on the inclined-plane section is W1=μmg cosθ·L. Since L cosθ=x, W1=μmgx. On the horizontal plane, the magnitude of the friction force is f2=μmg, and the distance of the horizontal section is s-x, so W2=μmg(s-x). The total work done in overcoming friction is W=W1+W2=μmgx+μmg(s-x)=μmgs. Substituting μ=0.1, m=50 kg, g=10 m/s^2, s=100 m, gives W=0.1×50×10×100=5000 J.

The total work done in overcoming friction is W=W1+W2=μmgx+μmg(s-x)=μmgs. Substituting μ=0.1, m=50 kg, g=10 m/s^2, s=100 m, gives W=0.1×50×10×100=5000 J.
